newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar closes higher, lifted by interest rates.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar closes higher, lifted by interest rates.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed higher boosted by firming bond yields on Friday.
The currency opened at US$0.6937/44 and finished higher on 0.6943/50 at the close.
In what dealers described as a quiet day, strong buying out of Asia once again took the dollar up to its high of 0.6953. There still seems to a lot of demand out there, dealers said.
"Investment based on high short term interest rates is mainly what is encouraging the offshore buying," a senior dealer said.
On the Trade-Weighted Index, the currency closed at 65.76 from a 65.68 opening.
The kiwi traded in a range of 0.6939-0.6953 in the session.
Dealers said the currency closed with a firm tone.
"The dollar should continue to stay strong overnight in a range of about 60/40," one said.
"I expect that level to hold and push on towards the highs of 0.6970 next week"

The market will probably bide time until the pre-election economic and fiscal update on September 12 and the key Reserve Bank's economic projections on September 13. Most dealers expect the bank to hold the line on monetary policy while signalling an easing late in the year or early in 1997.
